book.principiamagica.principia.name: Principia
book.principiamagica.principia.the_wet_c: The scribe calls them *me*. I call them axioms: laws that need no proof, only obedience. Carve the purpose while the clay is wet, with something of that purpose pressed in: grain for the harvest, a sapling for the felling. Then fire it. Wet clay can still be persuaded. Fired clay cannot.

*Enki kept the decrees in his house in Eridu: the decree of the plough, the decree of the axe, the decree of kingship, the decree of the destruction of cities. Each could be held in the hand. Each could be given away.*

Clay holds a law, but law alone does not move. The old makers mixed in flesh: a god's, if the tablet is to be believed. I have only what the dead leave behind. It will have to do. I would rather not think about what the clay remembers of it.

*They slew We-ila, the god who had reason. In his flesh and blood they mixed the clay. From his flesh came the ghost, and the ghost remembered. So man was made, to bear the basket in the gods' place.*
Set a ball of clay in the catch trough and pour unguent over it. Wait while it listens. For every 25 mB of unguent it gives back two quickened clay.

Right-click a block face with the stylus to carve the first corner. Right-click a second face to carve the opposite corner. Together the two glyphs mark a rectangle, no wider and no deeper than 64 blocks, and every corner can be lifted later on its own.

Shift-right-click a carved glyph with the stylus to erase its boundary, and the field it belonged to is gone. You can do this from a distance: aim at a glyph and it glows, then shift-right-click it to erase. Shift-right-click inside a boundary also erases it. Breaking the block a glyph is carved into does not erase it. The glyph stays on the face where the block was, and the boundary holds until the stylus removes it.

With your golem selected, right-click a chest with the stylus to link it. Each further right-click changes the link: supply, then deposit, then both, then unlinked again. A supply chest gives the golem seeds, saplings and bone meal. A deposit chest takes the harvest. Shift-right-click a linked chest to remove its link at once, and the boundary around it stays as it is.
The chests touching the golem when it is given an axiom are linked both ways, so a golem placed beside its field and a chest works right away.
A chest is only a chest until the golem knows what to do with it. Let it fetch from one, and let it fill another. I do not need to touch either myself.

Hold shift and scroll over the body of a boundary to move all of it up or down at once. Its corners keep their blocks and move with it. A flat boundary stays flat, and the golem decides how far it reaches from its level.

The old landholders carved their boundaries in stone and cursed whoever moved them. My golem needs only the marks. Carved corners tell it where its field begins and ends; it decides how high to reach unless I lift the boundary myself.

Hold shift and scroll over a corner glyph with the stylus to lift that corner. It rises on its own plumb line, from the block it was carved into. A corner can be lifted up to sixteen blocks, or sunk down to eight blocks below its block. When the corners sit at different heights, the boundary is a box, and the golem works the whole box, reaching as far as its axiom allows.

Right-click a glyph with the stylus to pick it up. The corner follows your crosshair. Right-click a block to carve it there again, and the boundary takes the new corner, keeping its lift. Right-click air to cancel, and the boundary goes back where it was.
*This is the boundary of the field. Whoever moves this stone, whoever says "the field is not bounded", may the gods of the land curse him, may his name be torn out.*
Right-click your golem with the stylus to select it. Right-click it again to deselect it. Only the selected golem shows its boundaries while you hold the stylus.
The clay by the river bears marks: wedges, rows of them, too regular to be chance. I have started copying them here. If they are words, someone meant them to last.
*In the beginning the gods laboured, and the labour was heavy. They dug the rivers. They bore the baskets. And they wept beneath the weight.*
Hold a fired axiom and right-click your golem. The axiom sinks into the clay and is spent. A golem that holds an axiom is no longer purposeless: it sets to work at once.

**Work** makes the golem do its job inside its work area.
\
\
**Follow** makes it walk after you.
\
\
**Stay** keeps it in place. A golem without an axiom can only follow or stay.
I pressed the axiom against its chest and the clay took it like a mouth. It went to the field at once. It has not looked at me since.

Shift-right-click your golem with an empty hand, or remove the axiom in its screen. The axiom returns to your hands and the golem is purposeless again. It stays where it is, unless it was set to follow you.
Right-click your golem with an empty hand to open its screen. There you set its mode, its work area and its links to containers.
*Let him bear the toil of the gods. Let him bear the basket.*

Without a work area of its own, a golem given an axiom marks a field of nine by nine blocks around the spot where it stands, one block down and two up. Containers touching the golem are linked to it and serve as both supply and deposit.
\
\
A field and a chest beside the golem are enough. A work area you have already set up is kept.
Wood for the bones, quickened clay for the sinews. When I set it down it turned its head toward me. Nothing more. It does not know what it is for. It only knows that I am here.

Place the golem on a block face and it stands there for good. It never wanders off and it never fades.
\
\
Without an axiom it has no purpose. It stays where it is put, or follows you if you ask it to. It cannot work until it is given an axiom.
*Fourteen pieces of clay she pinched off. Seven on the right, seven on the left. Between them she set the brick.*
A cut reed would do, but copper holds its edge. With this I can carve the clay, and, if the tablets are right, command what the clay holds.
*The reed is cut, the clay is wet, the word goes in. What is pressed in the clay does not leave it.*

As a crafting tool, the stylus is never consumed: it returns to your grid after every recipe that uses it.
\
\
As a configuration tool, it selects a golem, carves, lifts and moves its work boundaries, and links its containers.
A blank tablet, pressed from quickened clay and held together with a stylus. The scribe treats wet clay as something that *listens*.
*Wet clay is open. It takes the word and the thumbprint and the fly that lands on it. Do not let it hear what you do not mean.*

job_option.principiamagica.bonemeal.desc: Use bone meal on crops that can still grow. Bone meal is restocked from supply containers.
job_option.principiamagica.bonemeal_sapl: Use bone meal on saplings in the work area so trees grow faster. Bone meal is restocked from supply containers.
Break natural leaves around a trunk when they stop the golem from reaching it. Player-placed leaves are never broken.
job_option.principiamagica.clear_obstruc: Clear grass, flowers and similar plants from the work area so crops can be planted. Seeds dropped by grass go into the golem's inventory.
Pick up loose items inside the work zone and deposit them.
job_option.principiamagica.replant.descr: Plant a seed on empty farmland after harvesting, preferring the seed that grew there before.
job_option.principiamagica.replant_sapli: Plant a matching sapling on the stump of each felled tree. Saplings are restocked from supply containers.
job_option.principiamagica.till.descript: Turn dirt and grass near water into farmland. Needs a hoe in the main hand and uses its durability.

principle.principiamagica.alabaster.desc: Translucent stone that holds light in solid mass.
principle.principiamagica.ash.descriptio: Severing. The dryness and edge of things that have ended.
principle.principiamagica.bitumen.descri: A dark mineral pitch that seals and binds.
principle.principiamagica.gleam.descript: Radiance. The clarity of sky, light and polished things.
principle.principiamagica.kohl.descripti: A pigment of soot and minerals.
principle.principiamagica.marrow.descrip: Living vitality kept in dry bone.
principle.principiamagica.sap.descriptio: Vitality. The growth and moisture of plants and flesh.
principle.principiamagica.silt.descripti: Foundation. The weight and permanence of earth, stone and clay.
principle.principiamagica.sinew.descript: Living tissue that binds a body together.
principle.principiamagica.unguent.descri: A fermented anointing oil that quickens clay.
research_fact.principiamagica.golem_give: Hold a fired axiom and right-click the golem with it.
research_fact.principiamagica.golem_plac: A body must stand on its own before it can be given a purpose.
tooltip.principiamagica.copper_stylus.hi: Shift-right-click air: clear selection and clipboard
Shift-right-click golem: copy workplace / paste clipboard
Right-click container: cycle supply, deposit, both, removed
Shift-left-click own golem: pick up (keeps workplace)
Right-click glyph: pick it up, right-click a block to place it again
Shift-scroll over a glyph: lift its corner. Over a footprint: move it up or down
Shift-right-click glyph or container: remove it
Right-click two block faces: carve a footprint
